question: What is TinkerOS?
answer: TinkerOS is a custom Linux-based operating system built on a real Linux kernel. It comes with three special modes called worlds, a built-in AI assistant, and over 224 system tools.

question: What are the three worlds?
answer: TinkerOS has three worlds: Game Station for gaming with max performance, Hackerspace for coding and development, and Normal for everyday use. You can switch between them anytime.

question: How do I switch worlds?
answer: Type tinker-world game for Game Station, tinker-world hack for Hackerspace, or tinker-world normal for Normal mode. You can also select the world at the login screen.

question: What is Game Station?
answer: Game Station is TinkerOS's gaming world. It automatically enables Game Mode, sets CPU to maximum performance, optimizes your GPU, and configures controller support. Great for gaming sessions.

question: What is Hackerspace?
answer: Hackerspace is the developer world in TinkerOS. It comes with code editors, terminal tools, Docker, and development environments pre-configured. Perfect for coding and programming.

question: How do I open the Control Center?
answer: Type tinkeros-control-center in the terminal or click the TinkerOS logo in the top-left corner of your screen. The Control Center has over 224 tools organized into categories like System, Gaming, Hardware, and more.

question: What is Searchie?
answer: Searchie is TinkerOS's personal search engine. It indexes your files, browser history, and documents so you can find anything instantly. Press Tab+F7 to open it, or type searchie in the terminal.

question: How do I search my files?
answer: Press Tab+F7 to open Searchie, then type what you're looking for. It searches through all your indexed files and shows results ranked by relevance. You can also use the terminal: searchie ask 'query'.

question: What is TinkerAI?
answer: TinkerAI is your built-in AI assistant, like Siri or Google Assistant but for your computer. Press Ctrl+Alt+Gr to open it, or type tinker-ai ask 'question' in the terminal. It can answer questions, control your computer, and help with tasks.

question: How do I open TinkerAI?
answer: Press Ctrl+Alt+Gr on your keyboard to open TinkerAI. You can also type tinker-ai ask 'your question' in the terminal. The AI pops up as a glassmorphism overlay at the top of your screen.

question: How do I enable Game Mode?
answer: Game Mode is automatic in the Game Station world. To enable it manually, type tinker-gamemode on in the terminal. To check if it's running, type tinker-gamemode status.

question: How do I take a screenshot?
answer: Type tinker-ai screenshot in the terminal, or use the standard Print Screen key. The screenshot is saved to your Pictures folder. You can also ask TinkerAI to take one for you.

question: How do I adjust the volume?
answer: Use the volume icon in the top-right system tray, or type tinker-audio volume 75 in the terminal to set it to 75%. You can also use the keyboard volume keys.

question: How do I change the brightness?
answer: Type tinker-display brightness 80 in the terminal to set brightness to 80%. You can also use the brightness keys on your keyboard, or adjust it in the Control Center under Display settings.

question: How do I open a browser?
answer: Type tinker-ai open firefox or tinker-ai open chrome in the terminal. You can also click the browser icon in your taskbar, or ask TinkerAI to open your browser for you.

question: How do I update TinkerOS?
answer: Type tinker-update in the terminal to check for and install updates. You can also use the Software Center app, or go to Control Center > System > Updates.

question: How do I backup my data?
answer: Type tinker-backup in the terminal to start the backup wizard. It will guide you through backing up your important files to an external drive or cloud storage.

question: What kernel modules does TinkerOS have?
answer: TinkerOS has custom kernel modules: thermal_sched for smart cooling, gamemode for gaming boost, energy_sched for battery saving, coil_whine for noise reduction, oled_wear for burn-in protection, and cache_tiering for performance.

question: How do I fix WiFi problems?
answer: First check: nmcli device status. If WiFi is disconnected, try: nmcli device wifi list to see available networks, then: nmcli device wifi connect 'NetworkName'. If that doesn't work, restart NetworkManager: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager.

question: How do I fix audio problems?
answer: Check your audio devices: pactl list sinks. Restart the audio system: pulseaudio -k && pulseaudio --start. To set a default device: pactl set-default-sink device-name. You can also check the Control Center > Sound settings.

question: How do I install new apps?
answer: You can install apps through the Software Center, Flatpak, or the terminal. For terminal: sudo apt install package-name. For Flatpak: flatpak install app-name. TinkerOS supports AppImage files too — just download and run them.

question: How do I customize the theme?
answer: Open Control Center > Customization. You can change themes, icons, fonts, and the glassmorphism effects. TinkerOS uses a glass design language with frosted glass and blur effects throughout the interface.

question: What is the glassmorphism design?
answer: Glassmorphism is TinkerOS's visual style — frosted glass panels with transparency, blur effects, rounded corners, and subtle shadows. It gives the desktop a modern, clean, and premium look.

question: How do I set a reminder?
answer: Open TinkerAI with Ctrl+Alt+Gr and say or type: remind me to take a break in 30 minutes. You can also use: tinker-ai remind 'message' 30m in the terminal.

question: How do I add a contact?
answer: Use TinkerAI: tinker-ai contact-add 'John Doe' '555-1234' 'john@email.com'. You can also manage contacts through the Contacts app in your application menu.

question: How do I check my battery?
answer: Look at the battery icon in the top-right system tray for a quick estimate. For detailed info, open Control Center > Hardware > Battery, or type tinker-battery status in the terminal.

question: How do I enable the firewall?
answer: Type tinker-firewall enable in the terminal. To check status: tinker-firewall status. You can also configure it through Control Center > Security > Firewall.

question: How do I clean up disk space?
answer: Type tinker-cleanup in the terminal. This will remove old packages, clear cache, and clean up temporary files. You can also use Control Center > System > Cleanup for a GUI option.

question: How do I run the dust dislodger?
answer: Type tinker-dust run in the terminal. This spins your fans at special intervals to dislodge dust from the vents. It's a maintenance feature to keep your cooling system working well.

question: What is the dust dislodger?
answer: The dust dislodger is a unique TinkerOS feature that spins your computer fans at carefully calculated speeds and intervals to shake loose dust from the cooling vents, helping maintain optimal airflow.

question: How do I check system temperature?
answer: Type sensors in the terminal to see CPU and GPU temperatures. You can also check through Control Center > Hardware > Temperature. TinkerOS's thermal_sched module manages cooling automatically.

question: How do I switch to dark mode?
answer: Open Control Center > Customization > Appearance and select Dark mode. Or type: gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme 'prefer-dark' in the terminal.

question: How do I open a terminal?
answer: Right click on the desktop and select 'Open Terminal', or press Ctrl+Alt+T, or search for 'Terminal' in the application menu.

question: What apps come with TinkerOS?
answer: TinkerOS includes a web browser, file manager, text editor, terminal, calculator, media player, email client, calendar, and over 224 system tools. It also has TinkerAI and Searchie built in.

question: How do I add a printer?
answer: Open Control Center > Hardware > Printers. Click 'Add Printer' and follow the wizard. TinkerOS supports most USB and network printers automatically.

question: How do I connect Bluetooth devices?
answer: Click the Bluetooth icon in the system tray, or open Control Center > Network > Bluetooth. Put your device in pairing mode, then click 'Pair' next to it in the list.

question: How do I set up a VPN?
answer: Open Control Center > Network > VPN. Click 'Add VPN' and enter your VPN provider's details. TinkerOS supports OpenVPN, WireGuard, and PPTP protocols.

question: What file system does TinkerOS use?
answer: TinkerOS uses ext4 as the default file system, which is the standard for Linux. It's reliable, fast, and well-tested. You can also use btrfs if you prefer snapshot support.

question: How do I resize a partition?
answer: Open Control Center > System > Disks, or use GParted. Be careful when resizing partitions — always backup your data first. Select the partition, click Resize, and apply changes.

question: How do I check for updates?
answer: Type tinker-update in the terminal, or open the Software Center app. TinkerOS will check for system updates, security patches, and app updates automatically.

question: How do I restart TinkerOS?
answer: Click the system menu in the top-right corner and select Restart, or type sudo reboot in the terminal. You can also press Ctrl+Alt+Delete if configured.

question: How do I shut down TinkerOS?
answer: Click the system menu in the top-right corner and select Shut Down, or type sudo shutdown now in the terminal. Hold the power button for 4 seconds as a last resort.

question: How do I create a new user?
answer: Open Control Center > System > Users, or type: sudo adduser newusername in the terminal. You can set the password and permissions during creation.

question: How do I change my password?
answer: Open Control Center > System > Users > Change Password, or type passwd in the terminal. You'll need to enter your current password first.

question: How do I enable automatic updates?
answer: Open Control Center > System > Updates and enable 'Automatic Updates'. You can choose to install security updates automatically while keeping other updates manual.

question: What programming languages are supported?
answer: TinkerOS comes with Python, Bash, and common development tools pre-installed. In the Hackerspace world, you also get Node.js, Rust, Go, and Java environments set up and ready to use.

question: How do I install Python packages?
answer: Use pip: pip install package-name. For system-wide installation: sudo pip install package-name. TinkerOS recommends using virtual environments: python -m venv myenv && source myenv/bin/activate.

question: How do I use Docker on TinkerOS?
answer: Docker is pre-installed in the Hackerspace world. Start it with: sudo systemctl start docker. Run containers: docker run -it ubuntu bash. Add your user to the docker group: sudo usermod -aG docker $USER.

question: How do I use Git on TinkerOS?
answer: Git is pre-configured. Clone a repo: git clone https://github.com/user/repo. Make changes, then: git add . && git commit -m 'message' && git push. TinkerOS has Git configured with sensible defaults.

question: What is the terminal multiplexer?
answer: TinkerOS uses tmux as the terminal multiplexer. It lets you have multiple terminal sessions in one window. Start it with: tmux. Split panes with Ctrl+B then % or ". Navigate with Ctrl+B then arrow keys.

question: How do I use tmux?
answer: Start tmux with: tmux. Create a new window: Ctrl+B then c. Split horizontally: Ctrl+B then ". Split vertically: Ctrl+B then %. Detach: Ctrl+B then d. Reattach: tmux attach.

question: How do I check my disk usage?
answer: Type df -h to see disk usage by partition. Use du -sh foldername to check a specific folder. Open Control Center > System > Storage for a visual overview with cleanup options.

question: How do I check my RAM usage?
answer: Type free -h to see RAM usage. Use top or htop for a real-time view. Open Control Center > System > Memory for a visual display of memory usage.

question: How do I check my CPU usage?
answer: Type top or htop in the terminal for real-time CPU monitoring. Use lscpu to see CPU info. Open Control Center > Hardware > CPU for a visual display.

question: How do I kill a frozen app?
answer: Try Alt+F4 to close the window normally. If that doesn't work, type xkill and click the frozen app. As a last resort, use: killall app-name or: kill $(pgrep app-name).

question: My computer is running slow
answer: Try these steps: 1) Check CPU usage with top or htop. 2) Close unused apps. 3) Run tinker-cleanup to free disk space. 4) Restart the computer. 5) Check for overheating with sensors. 6) Switch to Normal world if in Game Station.

question: My screen is black
answer: Try: 1) Press Ctrl+Alt+F2 to switch to a text terminal. 2) Login and type: sudo systemctl restart gdm3. 3) If that doesn't work, try: sudo apt update && sudo apt reinstall ubuntu-desktop. 4) Check cables if using external monitor.

question: My internet is not working
answer: Check: nmcli device status. Restart network: sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager. For WiFi: nmcli device wifi list && nmcli device wifi connect 'SSID'. For ethernet: check cable connection.

question: How do I enable encryption?
answer: TinkerOS supports full disk encryption during installation. For individual files, use: gpg -c filename to encrypt, gpg filename.gpg to decrypt. You can also use VeraCrypt for encrypted volumes.

question: How do I scan for viruses?
answer: TinkerOS includes ClamAV. Scan with: sudo clamscan -r /home. For real-time protection, enable ClamTK from Control Center > Security > Antivirus.

question: How do I check my network speed?
answer: Install speedtest-cli: sudo apt install speedtest-cli, then run: speedtest. Or open a browser and search for 'speed test' to use an online tool.

question: How do I set a static IP?
answer: Open Control Center > Network, select your connection, go to IPv4 settings, and change from Automatic to Manual. Enter your IP address, gateway, and DNS servers.

question: How do I use SSH?
answer: Connect to a remote server: ssh user@hostname. Generate SSH keys: ssh-keygen -t ed25519. Copy key to server: ssh-copy-id user@hostname. TinkerOS has SSH configured by default.

question: How do I use Flatpak?
answer: Search for apps: flatpak search app-name. Install: flatpak install app-name. Run: flatpak run app-name. List installed: flatpak list. Update: flatpak update.

question: How do I use AppImage?
answer: Download the .AppImage file, make it executable: chmod +x app.AppImage, then run it: ./app.AppImage. AppImages run without installation and can be stored anywhere.

question: What is the boot animation?
answer: TinkerOS has a custom Plymouth boot animation with a pulsing TinkerOS logo and progress bar. It shows during startup, shutdown, and reboot. The GRUB boot menu is also branded with the TinkerOS theme.

question: How do I change the boot theme?
answer: Open Control Center > Customization > Boot Theme, or use: Plymouth theme: sudo plymouth-set-default-theme TinkerOS. For GRUB: sudo update-grub after making changes.

question: How do I access the BIOS?
answer: Restart your computer and press the BIOS key during boot. Common keys: F2, F12, Del, Esc. The key depends on your motherboard manufacturer. TinkerOS will show a message during boot if you press Shift for GRUB.

question: How do I dual boot with Windows?
answer: Install Windows first, then TinkerOS. During TinkerOS installation, choose 'Install alongside Windows'. The GRUB boot menu will let you choose between TinkerOS and Windows at startup.

question: How do I recover deleted files?
answer: Check the Trash first. If emptied, try: sudo apt install testdisk && photorec. For git repos: git checkout HEAD -- filename. TinkerOS also has automatic backups if enabled.

question: How do I change the default browser?
answer: Open Control Center > System > Default Applications, and select your preferred browser. Or use: xdg-settings set default-web-browser browser.desktop.

question: How do I add a keyboard shortcut?
answer: Open Control Center > Customization > Keyboard Shortcuts. Click 'Add Shortcut', press your desired key combination, and assign it to an action or command.

question: How do I enable auto-login?
answer: Open Control Center > System > Users, select your user, and enable 'Automatic Login'. Be aware this reduces security if others have physical access to your computer.

question: How do I check system logs?
answer: Use journalctl for system logs: journalctl -xe for recent errors, journalctl -u service-name for specific services. Or open Control Center > System > Logs for a GUI viewer.

question: How do I use the clipboard history?
answer: Press Ctrl+V to paste, or Super+V to open the clipboard history panel. TinkerOS keeps a history of your copied items so you can paste older items.

question: How do I use multiple monitors?
answer: Connect your monitors, then open Control Center > Display. You can arrange them, set resolution, and choose between mirror or extend mode. Or use: xrandr to configure from terminal.

question: How do I record my screen?
answer: Type gnome-screenshot for screenshots, or use OBS Studio for video recording. Install OBS: sudo apt install obs-studio. It's available in the Software Center too.

question: How do I use virtual desktops?
answer: Press Super+Tab to switch between virtual desktops. Create new ones with Super+Ctrl+Up. Move windows between desktops by dragging them to the edge of the screen.

question: How do I enable do not disturb?
answer: Click the clock in the top bar to open the calendar panel, then toggle 'Do Not Disturb'. This silences all notifications until you turn it off.

question: How do I use night light?
answer: Open Control Center > Display > Night Light and enable it. It reduces blue light in the evening to help you sleep better. You can set the schedule and color temperature.

question: How do I manage startup apps?
answer: Open Control Center > System > Startup Applications. You can add, remove, or disable apps that start automatically when you log in.

question: How do I check my IP address?
answer: Type ip addr show in the terminal, or hostname -I for a quick view. Open Control Center > Network to see your IP in the GUI.

question: How do I open a specific file?
answer: Use the file manager (nautilus or thunar), or type: xdg-open filename in the terminal. TinkerAI can also open files for you: tinker-ai open filename.

question: How do I change the wallpaper?
answer: Right-click the desktop and select 'Change Wallpaper', or open Control Center > Customization > Appearance. TinkerOS includes several glassmorphism-themed wallpapers.

question: How do I enable touchpad gestures?
answer: Touchpad gestures are enabled by default. Use three-finger swipe up for activities, three-finger swipe left/right to switch desktops, and pinch to zoom in supported apps.

question: How do I use screen sharing?
answer: Install Zoom or Teams from the Software Center, or use the built-in GNOME Screen Sharing. Open Control Center > System > Screen Sharing to enable remote access.

question: How do I manage my power settings?
answer: Open Control Center > System > Power. You can set screen timeout, sleep timeout, and power button behavior. For more options, use: tinker-power save or tinker-power performance.

question: How do I check my GPU?
answer: Type lspci | grep VGA in the terminal. For NVIDIA GPUs: nvidia-smi. For detailed info: glxinfo | grep 'OpenGL renderer'. Open Control Center > Hardware > Graphics for more.

question: How do I install NVIDIA drivers?
answer: Open Control Center > Hardware > Graphics, or use: sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall. For specific version: sudo apt install nvidia-driver-535. Restart after installation.

question: How do I use Wayland?
answer: TinkerOS supports Wayland by default. If you need X11, select 'GNOME on Xorg' at the login screen. Most apps work on Wayland; check compatibility for specialized tools.

question: How do I use fractional scaling?
answer: For HiDPI displays: Settings > Displays > Scale. Choose 125%, 150%, or 175%. Or use: gsettings set org.gnome.mutter experimental-features "['scale-monitor-framebuffer']" for more options.

question: How do I enable location services?
answer: Open Control Center > Privacy > Location Services and enable it. Apps like weather and maps can then use your approximate location for better results.

question: How do I manage app permissions?
answer: Open Control Center > Privacy. You can control which apps have access to camera, microphone, location, files, and contacts. Toggle permissions per app.

question: How do I use parental controls?
answer: Open Control Center > Parental Controls. You can set screen time limits, block inappropriate content, and manage which apps children can use.

question: How do I use the built-in backup?
answer: Type tinker-backup in the terminal, or open Control Center > System > Backup. You can back up to an external drive, network location, or configure automatic backups.

question: How do I restore from backup?
answer: Open Control Center > System > Backup > Restore, or use: tinker-backup restore in the terminal. Select your backup file and follow the wizard to restore your data.

question: How do I check my system specs?
answer: Type neofetch in the terminal for a quick overview. Or use: lscpu for CPU, free -h for RAM, lsblk for disks, lspci for hardware. Open Control Center > Hardware > System Info for a GUI.

question: How do I overclock my CPU?
answer: Open Control Center > Hardware > CPU > Overclocking. Be careful — overclocking can cause instability and overheating. TinkerOS monitors temperatures and will throttle if things get too hot.

question: How do I undervolt my CPU?
answer: Use: sudo intel-undervolt apply in the terminal, or configure through Control Center > Hardware > CPU > Power. Undervolting reduces power consumption and heat while maintaining performance.

question: How do I check my SSD health?
answer: Type: sudo smartctl -a /dev/sda in the terminal. Look for 'Reallocated Sector Count' and 'Wear Leveling'. Open Control Center > Hardware > Storage for a visual health display.

question: How do I enable TRIM for SSD?
answer: TRIM is enabled by default on TinkerOS. Verify with: systemctl status fstrim.timer. If not running: sudo systemctl enable --now fstrim.timer.

question: How do I use ZFS on TinkerOS?
answer: Install ZFS: sudo apt install zfsutils-linux. Create a pool: sudo zpool create tank /dev/sdb. Create datasets: sudo zfs create tank/data. ZFS provides snapshots, compression, and data integrity.

question: How do I use LVM?
answer: LVM is available during installation. For existing installs: sudo apt install lvm2. Create physical volumes: sudo pvcreate /dev/sdb. Create volume group: sudo vgcreate data /dev/sdb. Create logical volumes: sudo lvcreate -n backup -L 50G data.

question: How do I use RAID?
answer: TinkerOS supports software RAID through mdadm. Install: sudo apt install mdadm. Create array: sudo mdadm --create /dev/md0 --level=1 --raid-devices=2 /dev/sdb /dev/sdc. Monitor: cat /proc/mdstat.

question: How do I use the firewall?
answer: TinkerOS uses UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall). Enable: sudo ufw enable. Allow SSH: sudo ufw allow ssh. Check status: sudo ufw status. Block an IP: sudo ufw deny from IP.

question: How do I use Fail2Ban?
answer: Install: sudo apt install fail2ban. Enable: sudo systemctl enable --now fail2ban. It automatically bans IPs with too many failed login attempts. Check banned IPs: sudo fail2ban-client status.

question: How do I use encryption for files?
answer: Use GPG: gpg -c filename to encrypt, gpg filename.gpg to decrypt. For full disk encryption, choose the option during TinkerOS installation. For USB drives: veracrypt or luksFormat.

question: How do I use Tor?
answer: Install: sudo apt install tor. Start: sudo systemctl start tor. Configure browser to use SOCKS5 proxy at 127.0.0.1:9050. Or install Tor Browser from the Software Center.

question: How do I use a VPN?
answer: Open Control Center > Network > VPN. Click Add VPN and enter your provider details. Or install: sudo apt install network-manager-openvpn-gnome for OpenVPN support.

question: How do I check for rootkits?
answer: Install: sudo apt install rkhunter chkrootkit. Run: sudo rkhunter --check, or sudo chkrootkit. Schedule regular scans with cron for automatic detection.

question: How do I use ClamAV?
answer: Install: sudo apt install clamav clamav-daemon. Update definitions: sudo freshclam. Scan: sudo clamscan -r /home. Real-time protection: sudo systemctl enable --now clamav-daemon.

question: How do I use AppArmor?
answer: AppArmor is enabled by default. Check status: sudo aa-status. Enforce a profile: sudo aa-enforce /etc/apparmor.d/profile-name. Disable: sudo ln -s /etc/apparmor.d/profile-name /etc/apparmor.d/disable/.

question: How do I use SELinux?
answer: SELinux is not the default on TinkerOS (it uses AppArmor). If needed: sudo apt install selinux-basics selinux-policy-default. Configure: sudo selinux-activate.

question: How do I use audit logs?
answer: Install: sudo apt install auditd. Monitor files: sudo auditctl -w /etc/passwd -p wa -k password-changes. View logs: sudo ausearch -k password-changes. Report: sudo aureport.

question: How do I use systemd?
answer: Check services: systemctl list-units. Start/stop: sudo systemctl start/stop service. Enable at boot: sudo systemctl enable service. View logs: journalctl -u service.

question: How do I use cron jobs?
answer: Edit crontab: crontab -e. Add a job: 0 9 * * * /path/to/script. Syntax: minute hour day month weekday command. List jobs: crontab -l. Remove all: crontab -r.

question: How do I use aliases?
answer: Edit ~/.bashrc and add: alias ll='ls -la'. Reload: source ~/.bashrc. Or add to ~/.bash_aliases for cleaner organization. Common aliases: ls, grep, update, upgrade.

question: How do I use environment variables?
answer: Set temporarily: export MY_VAR=value. Set permanently: add to ~/.bashrc. View all: env or printenv. View specific: echo $MY_VAR. Unset: unset MY_VAR.

question: How do I use SSH keys?
answer: Generate: ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'your@email.com'. Copy to server: ssh-copy-id user@server. Connect: ssh user@server (no password needed). Keys are more secure than passwords.

question: How do I use rsync?
answer: Sync folders: rsync -avz /source/ /dest/. Preview: rsync -avzn /source/ /dest/. Exclude: rsync -avz --exclude='*.log' /source/ /dest/. Remote: rsync -avz /source/ user@host:/dest/.

question: How do I use vim?
answer: Open file: vim filename. Insert mode: i. Save and quit: Esc then :wq. Quit without save: Esc then :q!. Delete line: dd. Search: /pattern. Vim is pre-installed on TinkerOS.

question: How do I use grep?
answer: Search in file: grep 'pattern' filename. Recursive search: grep -r 'pattern' directory. Case insensitive: grep -i 'pattern' file. Show line numbers: grep -n 'pattern' file.

question: How do I use find?
answer: Find files: find /path -name 'filename'. Find by type: find . -type f -name '*.txt'. Find by size: find . -size +100M. Find modified today: find . -mtime 0.

question: How do I use sed?
answer: Replace text: sed -i 's/old/new/g' filename. Delete lines: sed -i '/pattern/d' file. Insert line: sed -i '3a\new line' file. View without editing: sed 's/old/new/g' file.

question: How do I use awk?
answer: Print column: awk '{print $1}' file. Filter: awk '$3 > 100' file. Custom delimiter: awk -F: '{print $1}' /etc/passwd. Combine: awk '{sum+=$1} END {print sum}' file.

question: How do I use curl?
answer: Download: curl -O URL. POST data: curl -d 'data' URL. Follow redirects: curl -L URL. Save output: curl -o file URL. With headers: curl -H 'Header: Value' URL.

question: How do I use wget?
answer: Download: wget URL. Recursive download: wget -r URL. Limit speed: wget --limit-rate=200k URL. Resume: wget -c URL. Background: wget -b URL.

question: How do I use tar?
answer: Create archive: tar -czf archive.tar.gz folder/. Extract: tar -xzf archive.tar.gz. List contents: tar -tzf archive.tar.gz. Extract to specific dir: tar -xzf archive.tar.gz -C /path/.

question: How do I use zip?
answer: Create: zip -r archive.zip folder/. Extract: unzip archive.zip. List contents: unzip -l archive.zip. Extract to dir: unzip archive.zip -d /path/.

question: How do I use make?
answer: Build project: make. Install: sudo make install. Clean: make clean. Specific target: make target. Read Makefile first to understand available targets.

question: How do I use cmake?
answer: Create build dir: mkdir build && cd build. Configure: cmake .. Build: make. Install: sudo make install. Clean: rm -rf build/ and start over.

question: How do I use docker compose?
answer: Start services: docker-compose up -d. Stop: docker-compose down. View logs: docker-compose logs. Rebuild: docker-compose up --build. List services: docker-compose ps.

question: How do I use kubernetes?
answer: Apply config: kubectl apply -f file.yaml. Get pods: kubectl get pods. Describe: kubectl describe pod name. Logs: kubectl logs pod-name. Delete: kubectl delete -f file.yaml.

question: How do I create a git repository?
answer: Initialize: git init. Add files: git add .. First commit: git commit -m 'initial commit'. Add remote: git remote add origin URL. Push: git push -u origin main.

question: How do I resolve merge conflicts?
answer: Open conflicting files and look for <<<<<<, =======, =======. Choose which changes to keep, delete the conflict markers, then: git add filename && git commit.

question: How do I use git branches?
answer: Create: git branch branch-name. Switch: git checkout branch-name. Create and switch: git checkout -b branch-name. List: git branch. Delete: git branch -d branch-name.

question: How do I use python?
answer: Run script: python3 script.py. Interactive: python3. Install packages: pip install package. Create virtual env: python3 -m venv env && source env/bin/activate.

question: How do I use node.js?
answer: Run script: node script.js. Install packages: npm install package. Init project: npm init. Start server: node server.js. Use npx for one-off commands.

question: How do I use rust?
answer: Install: curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh. Create project: cargo new project. Build: cargo build. Run: cargo run.

question: How do I use go?
answer: Install: sudo snap install go --classic. Create project: mkdir project && cd project && go mod init project. Build: go build. Run: go run main.go.

question: How do I use mysql?
answer: Install: sudo apt install mysql-server. Secure: sudo mysql_secure_installation. Login: mysql -u root -p. Create database: CREATE DATABASE name; Use: USE name;

question: How do I use postgresql?
answer: Install: sudo apt install postgresql. Login: sudo -u postgres psql. Create database: CREATE DATABASE name; Create user: CREATE USER name WITH PASSWORD 'pass';

question: How do I use redis?
answer: Install: sudo apt install redis-server. Start: sudo systemctl start redis. Connect: redis-cli. Set value: SET key value. Get value: GET key. List keys: KEYS *.

question: How do I use nginx?
answer: Install: sudo apt install nginx. Start: sudo systemctl start nginx. Config: /etc/nginx/sites-available/default. Test: nginx -t. Reload: sudo systemctl reload nginx.

question: How do I use apache?
answer: Install: sudo apt install apache2. Start: sudo systemctl start apache2. Config: /etc/apache2/sites-available/. Enable site: sudo a2ensite site.conf. Reload: sudo systemctl reload apache2.

question: How do I use logrotate?
answer: Config in /etc/logrotate.d/. Example: /var/log/app.log { daily rotate 7 compress }. Test: logrotate -d config. Force rotation: logrotate -f config.

question: How do I use screen?
answer: Start: screen -S name. List: screen -ls. Attach: screen -r name. Detach: Ctrl+A then D. Kill: screen -X -S name quit. Split: Ctrl+A then S.

question: How do I use byobu?
answer: Start: byobu. New window: F2. Switch windows: F3/F4. Detach: F6. Status bar: F12. Byobu is an enhanced screen/tmux wrapper pre-installed on TinkerOS.

question: How do I use zsh?
answer: Switch default: chsh -s /bin/zsh. Install oh-my-zsh: sh -c '$(curl -fsSL https://raw.github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/master/tools/install.sh)'. Config: ~/.zshrc.

question: How do I use fzf?
answer: Install: sudo apt install fzf. Use: type ** then Tab for fuzzy completion. Search history: Ctrl+R. Search files: find . | fzf. Kill process: kill $(ps aux | fzf).

question: How do I use ripgrep?
answer: Install: sudo apt install ripgrep. Search: rg 'pattern' directory. Case insensitive: rg -i 'pattern'. File types: rg -t py 'pattern'. Replace: rg 'old' -r 'new' file.

question: How do I use fd?
answer: Install: sudo apt install fd-find. Find files: fd pattern. Find by extension: fd -e py. Find by type: fd -t d (directories). Ignore: fd --exclude node_modules.

question: How do I use bat?
answer: Install: sudo apt install bat. View file: bat file.py. Line numbers: bat -n file.py. Language detect: bat --list-languages. Diff: bat --diff file1 file2.

question: How do I use exa?
answer: Install: sudo apt install exa. List: exa. Tree: exa --tree. Long format: exa -l. Git status: exa -l --git. Sort by size: exa --sort=size.

question: How do I use delta?
answer: Install: sudo apt install git-delta. Configure git: git config --global core.pager delta. View diffs: git diff. Features: syntax highlighting, line numbers, side-by-side.

question: How do I use lazygit?
answer: Install: sudo apt install lazygit. Run: lazygit. Navigate with arrow keys. Stage files: Space. Commit: c. Push: P. Pull: p. Quit: q. It's a terminal UI for git.

question: How do I use httpie?
answer: Install: sudo apt install httpie. GET: http URL. POST: http POST URL name=john. Headers: http URL Authorization:Bearer token. JSON: http POST URL json:={"key":"value"}.

question: How do I use jq?
answer: Install: sudo apt install jq. Pretty print: cat file.json | jq. Filter: jq '.name' file.json. Array: jq '.[0]' file.json. Multiple: jq '{name, age}' file.json.

question: How do I use yq?
answer: Install: sudo snap install yq. Read: yq '.metadata.name' file.yaml. Write: yq -i '.key = "value"' file.yaml. Convert: yq -o json file.yaml. Delete: yq -i 'del(.key)' file.yaml.

question: How do I use neovim?
answer: Install: sudo apt install neovim. Open: nvim file. Insert: i. Save: :w. Quit: :q. Install plugins: use lazy.nvim or vim-plug. Config: ~/.config/nvim/init.lua.

question: How do I use podman?
answer: Install: sudo apt install podman. Run: podman run -it ubuntu bash. Build: podman build -t name . Rootless: no sudo needed. Podman is a Docker alternative.

question: How do I use terraform?
answer: Install: sudo snap install terraform. Init: terraform init. Plan: terraform plan. Apply: terraform apply. Destroy: terraform destroy. State: terraform state list.

question: How do I use ansible?
answer: Install: sudo apt install ansible. Ping hosts: ansible all -m ping. Run playbook: ansible-playbook playbook.yml. Ad-hoc: ansible all -m shell -a 'uptime'.

question: How do I use vagrant?
answer: Install: sudo apt install vagrant. Init: vagrant init ubuntu/bionic64. Start: vagrant up. SSH: vagrant ssh. Stop: vagrant halt. Destroy: vagrant destroy.

question: How do I use cron?
answer: Edit crontab: crontab -e. Run daily at 9am: 0 9 * * * /path/to/script. Run every hour: 0 * * * * command. Run weekly: 0 9 * * 0 command. View: crontab -l.

question: How do I use systemd timers?
answer: Create .timer and .service files in /etc/systemd/system/. Enable: sudo systemctl enable timer-name. Start: sudo systemctl start timer-name. Check: systemctl list-timers.

question: What is the version of TinkerOS?
answer: TinkerOS v1.3.0 runs on Linux 6.x with 27 custom kernel modules. It uses a GNOME desktop with glassmorphism theming, is based on Ubuntu/Debian, and ships as a ~7.6 GB bootable ISO.

question: How do I check TinkerOS version?
answer: Type tinker-version in the terminal, or check the 'About' section in Control Center > System. You can also view neofetch output for detailed version information.

question: What license does TinkerOS use?
answer: TinkerOS uses the Dual Source License v1.0. Option A is public (open source), Option B is private (closed source). Both options are available at no fee.

question: How do I download TinkerOS?
answer: TinkerOS is available as a bootable ISO (~7.6 GB) from SourceForge: https://sourceforge.net/projects/tinkeros/files/v1.3/TinkerOS-v1.3.iso/. Flash it to a USB drive and boot from it.

question: How do I install TinkerOS?
answer: Flash the ISO to a USB drive using Balena Etcher or dd. Boot from the USB, follow the installer. You can install alongside Windows (dual boot) or use the entire disk.

question: How do I check TinkerOS world status?
answer: Type tinker-world status in the terminal to see which world is currently active. You can also look at the world indicator in the top bar of your desktop.

question: How do I use panic wipe?
answer: Press Space+Shift+Escape to trigger a panic wipe. This is an emergency feature that wipes sensitive data. Use with caution — it's irreversible.

question: What is NORMAL world?
answer: NORMAL is the most protected world in TinkerOS. It's for everyday use — standard desktop with all productivity apps. It can find/hack the user but CANNOT be hacked. It has 14 territory tools including app-allowlist, biometric-lock, and vault-engine.

question: What is HACK world?
answer: HACK is the world that protects the hacker while helping them hack. Only Tor Browser works here, and only safe approved apps may run. It includes 18 territory tools like amnesia-firewall, kill-switch, and threat-monitor.

question: What is GAME world?
answer: GAME is the maximum performance gaming world. It sets CPU perf governor to max, enables low-latency scheduler, optimizes GPU/IO priority, and activates GameMode. It has 13 territory tools including gpu-lock, frame-pacing, and game-replay-ai.

question: How do I use territory tools?
answer: Territory tools are pre-configured for each world. Access them through Control Center > Territory Tools, or run them from the terminal. Each world has its own set of tools optimized for that environment.

question: What territory tools are in GAME world?
answer: GAME world has 13 tools: anticheat-consent, audio-focus, controller-haptics, frame-pacing, game-mode, game-replay-ai, game-studio, gpu-lock, latency-clean, lowlat-input, perf-tune, save-archiver, and spectator-box.

question: What territory tools are in HACK world?
answer: HACK world has 18 tools: amnesia-firewall, app-guard, browser-gate, canary-honeypot, ephemeral-ram, gpu-pipeline, hack-defense, hack-gate, hack-mode, hack-ways, intent-hardware, kill-switch, masked-proc, panic-wipe, portal-sandbox, reverse-proxy, sdr-isolation, split-personality, supply-chain, threat-monitor.

question: What territory tools are in NORMAL world?
answer: NORMAL world has 14 tools: app-allowlist, biometric-lock, canary-monitor, duress-alert, filevault2, gatekeeper2, identity-cloud, key-wallet, privacy-ledger, secure-mode, sip-guard, traffic-guard, vault-engine, zero-trust-config.

question: How do I use the zero latency input?
answer: The zero_latency_input kernel module is active in GAME world. It provides ultra-low-latency input handling for gaming. It's automatic — no configuration needed when in GAME world.

question: How do I use OLED protection?
answer: The oled_wear kernel module automatically shifts pixels to prevent burn-in on OLED screens. It's active by default. Check status in Control Center > Hardware > OLED Protection.

question: How do I use cache tiering?
answer: The cache_tiering kernel module optimizes CPU cache usage automatically. It's active in all worlds. You can adjust settings in Control Center > Hardware > Cache Tiering.

question: How do I use thermal scheduling?
answer: The thermal_sched kernel module manages smart thermal cooling with user hints. It's active by default. It adjusts fan speeds and CPU throttling based on temperature. Check in Control Center > Hardware > Thermal.

question: How do I use energy scheduling?
answer: The energy_sched kernel module is a battery saver that adapts to your usage patterns. It's active in NORMAL world. It optimizes power consumption automatically.

question: How do I use coil whine reduction?
answer: The coil_whine kernel module uses spread-spectrum technology to reduce coil whine noise. It's active by default. No configuration needed — it works silently in the background.

question: How do I calibrate the dust dislodger?
answer: Before using the dust dislodger, calibrate it first: tinker-dust calibrate. This calculates the fan rated ceiling, RPM-per-PWM slope, and stall-floor for your specific hardware.

question: How do I use the hardware fingerprinting?
answer: The hardware_dna kernel module fingerprints your hardware for security purposes. It's used by NORMAL world's security tools to verify system integrity. Check status in Control Center > Security > Hardware DNA.

question: How do I use software-defined GPU?
answer: The sdgpu kernel module provides software-defined GPU capabilities. It allows dynamic GPU resource allocation. Configure through Control Center > Hardware > GPU > Software Defined.

question: How do I use FPGA scaler?
answer: The fpga_scaler kernel module provides FPGA-based hardware scaling. It's an advanced feature for hardware acceleration. Configure through Control Center > Hardware > FPGA Scaler.

question: How do I use CXL memory?
answer: The cxl_memory kernel module provides CXL (Compute Express Link) memory support. It's for systems with CXL-compatible hardware. Configure through Control Center > Hardware > CXL Memory.

question: How do I use predictive prewarm?
answer: The predictive_prewarm kernel module intelligently preloads data based on usage patterns. It improves application launch times by predicting what you'll need. Active by default in all worlds.

question: How do I use smart power grid?
answer: The smart_power_grid kernel module optimizes power distribution across system components. It balances performance and efficiency. Active by default — no manual configuration needed.

question: How do I use adaptive display?
answer: The adaptive_display kernel module adjusts display settings based on content and environment. It optimizes brightness, contrast, and color temperature. Configure in Control Center > Display > Adaptive.

question: How do I use unified memory?
answer: The unified_memory kernel module provides unified memory management across CPU and GPU. It improves data transfer efficiency for graphics-intensive tasks. Active in GAME world by default.

question: How do I use hardware tuning?
answer: The hardware_tuning kernel module provides fine-grained hardware control. Access through Control Center > Hardware > Hardware Tuning. It allows adjusting CPU, GPU, and memory parameters.

question: How do I use neural super resolution?
answer: The neural_super_res kernel module uses AI to upscale images and video in real-time. It improves visual quality without the performance cost of native resolution. Active in GAME world.

question: How do I use predictive rendering?
answer: The predictive_render kernel module predicts and pre-renders upcoming frames to reduce latency. It's optimized for gaming in GAME world. Active automatically when gaming.

question: How do I use remote hardware API?
answer: The remote_hardware_api kernel module allows remote access to hardware resources. It's for advanced users who need to control hardware remotely. Configure through Control Center > Advanced > Remote HW API.

question: How do I use finance audit?
answer: The finance_audit kernel module provides financial data auditing capabilities. It's used by NORMAL world's vault-engine and privacy-ledger tools for secure financial tracking.
